current_advisory.precondition_source: The linked original OSV details name untrusted model import/export paths with pathsec enforcement; this review grants no arbitrary-code or model-file operation.

gpt-researcher.meaning: Fresh bounded static source observation of the installed pinned closure and current recipe. Names alone do not prove call reachability; prior source review checks the entered nltk modules and their call sites.

crawl4ai.meaning: Fresh bounded static source observation of the installed pinned closure and current recipe. Names alone do not prove call reachability; prior source review checks the entered nltk modules and their call sites.

scope_decision.reason: The pinned current recipes and documented direct callers use tokenization/corpora/data management, not the advisory model import/export APIs. Existing prior reviews describe exact entered modules and limitations; the fresh check above independently binds current installed source and recipe. The existing ignore stays hash-scoped, with its existing expiry and no new ignore IDs.
scope_decision.approval_scope: Source-based non-reachability for these exact locks/recipes only; no proof against dynamic imports, new MCP tools or worker-authored arbitrary code.

corrections.mistake: A historical GPT source-review sentence referred to an existing scoped guard allowance before it was registered.
corrections.verification: Native ignore-policy unittest exit 1 on 2026-09-30; original guard lacks both new locks.
corrections.change: This dated review registers the exact two current lock hashes only after source observation; prior assertion is treated as proposed at its capture date.

limits: No vulnerable model-artifact API was invoked and no exploit test was performed.
The original detailed reviews used hash-verified wheels; this new check inspects installed Python source and does not claim a complete new binary/wheel audit.
The global existing ignore alone is not acceptance; its independent guard must pass.
OpenHands findings require a supported lock repair; no new suppression is granted for them.
Image scans and live runtime acceptance remain separate.
Provider and whole-task usage are unknown; no model call or saving comparison was made.

Expiry plan: the OpenHands lock was relocked onto PyJWT 2.14.0 on 2026-09-30 and still pins oauthlib 3.3.1; as of 2026-09-30, oauthlib 4.0.0 (PyPI, 2026-09-28T06:01Z) was inside the 7-day window the upstream workspace's exclude-newer applies (until 2026-10-05T06:01:19Z), so the relock onto it follows, tracked in #518 (owner: bc, session native-agent-stack-bc; earliest 2026-10-05T18:40:43Z, when PyJWT 2.15.1 has left its window too; due 2026-10-08), and in the same change deletes the OpenHands entry of IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS, whose sha256 pin fails any change to that lock. The Lumibot lock stays frozen on 3.3.1, so on 2026-10-13 renew this ignore for that lock alone with a new dated reason, or delete that lock.
GHSA-xpv3-w29h-x7cv and 1 alias have been filtered out because: oauthlib >= 3.0.0, < 4.0.0 (fixed in 4.0.0; the scanned locks pin 3.3.1): an oauthlib authorization server compares the PKCE code_verifier with == (code_challenge_method_s256 at oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/grant_types/authorization_code.py:49 and code_challenge_method_plain at :61, in 3.3.1), called only from AuthorizationCodeGrant.validate_token_request (line 506) when a token endpoint handles a request. Evidence: evidence/receipts/osv-oauthlib-pyjwt-reachability-20260929.json and, for the OpenHands lock at its relocked sha256, evidence/receipts/osv-openhands-pyjwt-relock-20260930.json. Expiry plan: as for GHSA-hj66-6f7g-4r5v; the OpenHands relock onto oauthlib 4.0.0 removes that lock's pin, and on 2026-10-13 this ignore is renewed for the frozen Lumibot lock alone or that lock is deleted.
